title: Implementation of dental monitoring to support home oral hygiene in adolescents undergoing fixed orthodontic treatment and adults undergoing systematic periodontal treatment – a clinical study
summary: The aim of this in vivo pilot study is to examine whether the use of the digital AI tool Dental Monitoring (Dental Monitoring, Paris, France) leads to an objectively measurable improvement in oral hygiene in adolescent orthodontic patients and adult periodontal patients. At the same time, a questionnaire will be used to clarify patients' subjective perceptions of the status of their oral hygiene.

interventions.name: Dental monitoring with home visualisation of plaque using plaque disclosing tablets and personalised advice on home oral hygiene
Dental monitoring without home visualisation of plaque using plaque disclosing tablets and personalised advice on home oral hygiene
Dental monitoring without home visualisation of plaque using plaque disclosing tablets and exclusively AI-based advice on home oral hygiene (no individual advice)
No dental monitoring, only oral hygiene instructions as part of normal check-ups

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria (orthodontic cohort)
• Patients with oral hygiene in need of improvement (plaque control record, PCR > 50%)
• Patients aged 12 to 17 years
• Patients receiving fixed orthodontic treatment with multibracket appliances or aligners
• Ability of the subject/legal guardian to understand the nature and individual consequences of the clinical study
• Written consent (from the legal guardian) after receiving information

Inclusion criteria (periodontitis cohort)
• Patients with oral hygiene in need of improvement (Plaque Control Record, PCR > 50%)
• Patients aged 30 years and older
• Patients with periodontitis, stage II-IV, grade A and B
• Ability of the subject to understand the nature and individual consequences of the clinical study
• Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Patients with a serious general illness
• Patients who do not have a smartphone
• Young people whose native language is not German
• Objection by legal guardians in the case of underage study participants (orthodontic cohort)
